prompt: Act as an adversarial reviewer in scientific computing, distributed systems, multiphysics coupling, and bubble dynamics. We have an existing GitHub Actions cluster with 12 independent ubuntu-latest runners plus an aggregation stage. We want to evolve it from embarrassingly parallel parameter sweeps into ONE coupled bubble-physics simulation in which different nodes own different physics modules and exchange feedback during the run. Proposed specialist roles include radial dynamics, gas thermodynamics, heat transfer, mass transfer, acoustics, interfacial/surfactant physics, shape modes, translation, wall/boundary effects, bubble-bubble interactions, turbulence/external flow, and a coordinator/stability/conservation node. Review whether this is physically and numerically defensible on GitHub Actions, where runners are ephemeral and not a low-latency MPI fabric. We care more about correct coupled dynamics than novelty. Recommend the best architecture under these constraints. Specifically answer: (1) which couplings require tight same-process or same-step integration and MUST NOT be distributed across slow network boundaries; (2) which couplings can safely use multirate/co-simulation exchange; (3) whether predictor-corrector, waveform relaxation, Jacobi/Gauss-Seidel partitioned coupling, operator splitting, or another method is best here and why; (4) how to prevent communication delay or asynchronous updates from creating fake oscillations/energy; (5) whether a shared state/event bus, artifact exchange, issue-based queue, external broker, or self-hosted runners would be appropriate; (6) the synchronization protocol, convergence criterion, rollback/timestep control, checkpoint format, and conservation checks; (7) how to map the 12 nodes by function, or whether a different decomposition is better; (8) what a scientifically defensible prototype should implement first; (9) a falsifiable validation plan comparing distributed vs monolithic reference integration; and (10) one hidden assumption most likely to make this architecture fail. Distinguish established numerical analysis from speculative design choices. Be concise but technically concrete. Review only; do not modify repository files.
context: Current core bubble hierarchy: Rayleigh-Plesset reference model and Keller-Miksis compressibility-aware model, with later thermal transport, dissolved gas/vapor transfer, shape modes, translation, Bjerknes interactions, many-bubble acoustics, and population/turbulence physics.

Existing cluster: GitHub Actions matrix worker IDs 0-11, max-parallel 12, each node writes a JSON artifact, aggregator combines results; current cluster is degradation-aware and can publish results transactionally.

Proposed communication concept: local microsteps on each specialist node, periodic state exchange, feedback correction, convergence check, accepted macrostep, repeat. We explicitly do NOT want network latency to become an unphysical delay term.
We can change the architecture if GitHub-hosted runners are the wrong substrate. Self-hosted runners or a hybrid local coordinator are acceptable recommendations if justified.
expected_response: A skeptical distributed-multiphysics architecture review with an implementable prototype design, synchronization algorithm, module partition, failure modes, and validation tests.
